context: Predecessor n0 stores 1 and successor n1 stores 3. Initially n0.next points to n1. The ellipsis to the right of n1 represents the rest of the list. The new node P stores 0 and has not yet been linked into the list. Here next is a pointer (reference) to a node's successor.
prose.result: All node values and all links after n1 stay the same. Given predecessor n0, updating the two references takes O(1) time and requires no movement of later nodes.

steps.announcement: The initial list is n0 (1) → n1 (3), with node P (0) ready for insertion.
steps.explanation: Initially, n0 (1) → n1 (3) → …, with n0.next pointing to n1. The new node P (0) is separate. The diagram does not show the initial target of P.next.
steps.key_state: Initially, n0.next = n1. Node P (value 0) is separate from the list.
steps.title: Initial links

steps.announcement: Execute P.next = n1 so that the new node P points to successor n1 first.
steps.explanation: Execute P.next = n1. The next references of n0 (1) and P (0) now both point to n1 (3). The links after n1 stay the same. Starting from n0 still leads directly to n1 without passing through P.
steps.key_state: After P.next = n1, n0.next still points to n1. Both references point to n1, and a traversal from n0 does not yet visit P.
steps.title: Link P to its successor

steps.announcement: Execute n0.next = P to finish insertion. The list becomes n0 (1) → P (0) → n1 (3) → remaining nodes.
steps.explanation: Execute n0.next = P, keeping P.next = n1. The links now form n0 (1) → P (0) → n1 (3) → …. From n0, a traversal visits P before continuing through the rest of the list. Insertion is complete.
steps.key_state: After n0.next = P, with P.next = n1, the final list is n0 (1) → P (0) → n1 (3) → ….
steps.title: Link P into the list

prose.summary: To insert a new node P between adjacent nodes n0 and n1, update just two references: first P.next, then n0.next.
prose.title: Inserting a node into a linked list

frames.explanation: First link the new node to the original successor, then point the predecessor to the new node. This keeps the rest of the list accessible. The code saves n0.next in n1 before executing the two assignments in the order shown. A traversal starting at n0 passes through P only after the second assignment.
